newsitem.title: UK: MSAS operating profits up 38 pct in H1 1996.
newsitem.headline: MSAS operating profits up 38 pct in H1 1996.

text.p: International logistics services company MSAS Cargo International Ltd said its operating profits grew 38 percent in the first six months of 1996 to 9.5 million stg ($14.8 million) , while turnover was five percent higher at 399 million stg.
MSAS is part of the London-based Ocean Group PLc industrial and distribution group.

"We still have a way to go to achieve our target of a three percent operating profit return in 1997 and will continue to maintain extremely competitive pricing for customers," MSAS Chief Executive Doug Ash said in a statement.
"Our operating profit for the last 12 months is 2.5 times that for 1993. This has been achieved not by acquisitions but by focusing single-mindedly on the needs of our customers," he added.

Against the background of the five percent growth in turnover, margins improved across all product areas. The absolute gross margin grew by 11 percent in the airfreight sector and by 23 percent for seafreight business.

The fastest growing sector continued to be warehousing, distribution and other supply chain services where the increase was 44 percent -- business in this sector has almost doubled in two years, the company said.
There was a further expansion of MSAS Logistics Services in Belgium, where the Sony group is a major customer, and where plans are now in hand to double capacity next year.
Other important developments were expanded services for Lucent Technologies in San Antonio,Texas and the management of Gillette Co's European warehousing activity near Frankfurt, the statement added.
Export air weight was static in North America and Europe, but continued growth was seen throughout the Asia-Pacific region, it noted.

In the U.S. margin and productivity improvements enabled MSAS to increase operating profits significantly despite the slow down in growth in the electronics sector. The Canadian business did not perform well in the first half, but a restructured organisation and recent business gains give MSAS grounds for optimism in the rest of the year, the statement said.
Europe produced strong operating profit growth, driven by excellent results in Germany, Italy and the UK. Operating profits also increased in France, Ireland and Norway, MSAS added

In South East Asia, all locations performed very strongly with Taiwan and Singapore leading the way. Japan's first half suffered in comparison with 1995 where the impact of the Kobe earthquake inflated airfreight volumes.
